newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki sags with Nokia, but bulls remain untamed.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki sags with Nokia, but bulls remain untamed.

text.p: Shares ended mixed with weakness in telecom group Nokia dragging the main indices lower on Thursday, though brokers said the softness looked temporary and a higher open for U.S. stocks pointed to further upside.
The FOX index fell 0.8 percent to 1,157.68, trimming but not wiping out Wednesday's gains of more than 1.6 percent. The all-share HEX fell 1.07 percent to 3,371.04 points.

"This is temporary, even if it could last a few days," one broker said. "We're so high that things are getting a bit shaky," said another, but nonetheless predicted a return to strength after the Dow industrials started higher in New York.
Volume was only fair, at 550 million markka.
Nokia fell 12.00 markka to close at 418.00, down almost three percent, after sturdy 200 million markka trade.
Brokers said profit-takers chewed away at Nokia's big gains on Wednesday, when it rose 17.50 markka, and the share was also knocked by an SBC Warburg downgrade to reduce from hold.
"It headed down immediately after the Warburg recommendation," one broker said.
But others played down the importance of the downgrade. "That's just one house among many," one said.

Forestry group UPM-Kymmene was one of several shares withstanding the session's weakness. It rose 1.10 markka to close at 133.10 after touching an all-time high 133.90 in hefty 70 million markka trade.

"Nokia's softness didn't hurt UPM at all," one broker said, and suggested it benfitted from the same bullishness that has lifted U.S. paper-makerss following this week's news of restructuring from International Paper and higher Q2 operating earnings from Georgia-Pacific.
Banking group Merita added 0.10 to return to 20.00, which brokers said still looks a tough resistance level.

Cargo handling and building materials group Partek ended 3.00 markka higher at 99.00 in lively 40 million markka volume, more than half of which stemmed from one 260,000-share deal matched inhouse by Carnegie at 99.00 per share.

Engineering group Metra's B share closed flat at 171.00 after 34 million markka trade, with most of the volume coming from one 145,000-share block deal brokered inhouse at AG Private Bankers at 170.00.
AG crossed the same number of Metra's A shares at 176.50 markka, up 2.50.
